portals.note: Page loaded but showed only an accessibility link in my fetch. No parcel or tax-bill search link was confirmed.

facts.summary: EPA reports that Forsite Development bought the Shelby facility, with its buildings and infrastructure, from Celanese under a sale/lease-back arrangement in 2021. The developer's project page describes the same deal and gives the facility as 420 acres.
facts.authority: U.S. EPA Superfund redevelopment page (secondary to a recorded deed; no deed checked)
facts.reference: Superfund Sites in Reuse in North Carolina
facts.quote: under a sale/lease-back arrangement with Celanese in 2021.

facts.summary: EPA reports that Forsite demolished much of the plant in 2022 while Ticona manufacturing continued on the site.
facts.reference: Superfund Sites in Reuse in North Carolina
facts.quote: It demolished much of the plant in 2022; manufacturing by Ticona continued.

facts.summary: CNA Holdings (Celanese) applied to renew NPDES wastewater permit NC0004952 for the Shelby Plant. The notice gives comments due June 22, 2026. The notice address (2525 Blacksburg Rd.) differs from the Superfund record (HWY 198), so this is matched by facility name, not address.
facts.reference: Comment Period Opens: CNA Holdings, LLC NPDES Permit NC0004952 (Celanese Shelby Facility)
facts.quote: CNA Holdings, LLC, 2525 Blacksburg Rd., Grover, N.C., has applied for a renewal of its NPDES wastewater permit (NC0004952)

gaps: Current owner not verified. The atlas owner GROVER INVESTMENTS I LLC was not checked against a parcel or deed record, and no parcel id is in the batch.
No recorded deed for the 2021 Forsite/Celanese sale was located. The Register of Deeds search was not run for this parcel.
Acreage conflict: EPA gives the Superfund site as 450 acres, Forsite gives the sold facility as 420 acres, and the batch shows 423.2. The sources do not explain the difference.
Address conflict: the Superfund record says HWY 198 and the DEQ notice says 2525 Blacksburg Rd. The link to this record rests on the facility name.
Shelby city permits and code enforcement were not searched. No 2022 demolition permit was located.
The Register of Deeds coverage start date conflicts: the county page says 1945, and an aggregator says the index starts in 1995. The county page was used.

facts.summary: EPA added the Davis Park Road TCE site to the National Priorities List in 1999, per EPA's redevelopment page.
facts.reference: Superfund Sites in Reuse in North Carolina
facts.quote: EPA added the site to the National Priorities List (NPL) in 1999.

facts.summary: EPA describes the Davis Park Road TCE Superfund site as 20 acres. The batch records 0.8 acres for this record.
facts.reference: Superfund Sites in Reuse in North Carolina
facts.quote: The 20-acre Davis Park Road TCE Superfund site is in Gastonia, North Carolina.

facts.summary: EPA reports that an auto repair shop remains in continued use on the site. The EPA page names an auto repair shop as the groundwater source.
facts.reference: Superfund Sites in Reuse in North Carolina
facts.quote: An auto repair shop remains in continued use on-site.

facts.summary: EPA reports that the Cedar Oak Park subdivision remains in continued use on the site.
facts.reference: Superfund Sites in Reuse in North Carolina
facts.quote: The Cedar Oak Park subdivision remains in continued use on-site.

facts.summary: EPA's site profile says the fifth Five-Year Review was being finalized and was expected to be completed by September 2025. Completion was not confirmed.
facts.reference: DAVIS PARK ROAD TCE site profile
facts.quote: The EPA is currently finalizing the fifth Five-Year Review status report.

gaps: Owner A TO Z RENTALS LLC and parcel 3534-76-4837 were not searched in the Gaston Tax Office or GIS viewer. The dynamic search was not run.
Acreage conflict: EPA gives the site as 20 acres and the batch records 0.8 acres for this record. The batch figure may be a single parcel; not reconciled.
The EPA site profile page does not state an EPA ID. The id 0405489 appears only in the URL parameter.
Five-Year Review completion (expected September 2025) was not confirmed.
The Register of Deeds was not searched for deeds or liens. The county says some older records are offline.
An older EPA snapshot (2017) appears in search results with conflicting NPL listing years (1999 and 2009). I did not open it; the current EPA page says 1999.

gaps: No parcel fact could be verified. The EPA cumulis profile for this site gives the name, EPA ID NYD980651087, and document collections, but no location, address, or acreage. It mentions only a repository address.
The EPA third Five-Year Review for the S-Area (semspub.epa.gov/work/HQ/179910.pdf) returned binary PDF content in this tool, so its location, size, and remedy statements are unverified.
No 2024-2026 S-Area documents were found. The Niagara Falls data center coverage (South End, about 53 acres) is not tied to the S-Area by any opened source, so it is not cited.
Acreage conflict: the batch records 169.5 acres. A court summary seen only in search results describes the S-Area as seven acres. Not reconciled.
Owner not searched. The atlas owner is null and state_parcel_layer is false. No Pros-GAR, deed, or lien search was run for Buffalo Avenue or the S-Area parcels.
